Cyber Attack Disrupts Payment Systems Across Uzbekistan, Impacting Businesses and Daily Life

TASHKENT – Businesses and consumers across Uzbekistan are facing widespread disruption today following a major cyber attack that has crippled the country’s electronic payments infrastructure. The incident, which began early Thursday morning, has left thousands of shops, restaurants, and service providers unable to process card payments, causing long queues, confusion, and mounting economic losses.

According to the Ministry of Digital Development, the attack targeted the central transaction processing system operated by UzPayNet, the nation’s largest payment gateway. While cash transactions remain possible, many urban businesses have reported significant drops in sales as customers struggle to access ATMs or switch to cash-only payments. Some banks have placed withdrawal limits in response to surging demand.

“We are working around the clock with cybersecurity experts to restore services and ensure the integrity of the payment system,” said Deputy Minister Dilshod Tulyaganov at a midday press briefing. “No customer funds have been lost, and all accounts remain secure, but we advise citizens to remain patient as we resolve the situation.”

The Chamber of Commerce estimates that over half of small businesses in Tashkent and Samarkand rely primarily on electronic payments. “This attack has hit retailers and market traders especially hard,” said chamber spokesperson Dilorom Iskandarova. “Many are losing an entire day’s takings. We urge the authorities to provide clear guidance and support.”

Telecommunications networks and essential services, including utilities and hospitals, report no direct impact so far, but several companies have warned of possible delays in salary disbursements and supplier payments if the outage persists.

Elbek Khasanov, an independent cybersecurity analyst based in Tashkent, called the attack “unprecedented in scale” for Uzbekistan. “It appears highly coordinated. The authorities must prioritize both recovery and a transparent investigation,” he said.

As of 5 p.m., authorities have not provided a timeline for full restoration of services. The State Security Service has launched a criminal investigation into the incident.
